title: Power Stack Watchlist
method: Fresh-money queue. Score and Action are separate. Strong themes do not automatically rank highly: the business must be able to fund itself, the valuation must leave room, and price should eventually confirm the thesis. Unverified creator/research leads contribute zero points.
marketRegime: Nominal and AI-led growth is still strong, but money is expensive and physical inputs remain tight. Prefer companies already turning demand into cash. Be more careful with businesses that need customers, suppliers or capital markets to finance the growth story.

buckets.label: Buy / Accumulate
buckets.description: Price, business quality and current theme setup are aligned enough for staged entry.

buckets.label: Selective / Retest
buckets.description: Good business/theme, but current price, tactical macro risk or overlap requires a better level or confirmation.

buckets.label: Wait / Confirm
buckets.description: Interesting exposure, but current risk/reward or cyclical timing is not strong enough to force.

buckets.label: Avoid / High Risk
buckets.description: Financing, valuation, dilution or execution risk currently dominates.

candidates.name: Micron Technology
candidates.entry: Research the next clean pullback or consolidation rather than chase a vertical move.
candidates.confirmation: HBM pricing and customer commitments stay firm while cash conversion remains strong.
candidates.invalidation: Cash generation weakens before supply catches up, or conventional-memory pricing rolls over hard.
candidates.thesis: AI systems need far more high-end memory, and Micron is already turning that shortage into cash. The question is no longer whether demand is strong. It is how long today's exceptional margins can last.

candidates.name: Cheniere Energy
candidates.entry: Prefer a pullback or stable base; do not chase an energy headline.
candidates.confirmation: Utilisation, contracts and distributable cash flow stay strong.
candidates.invalidation: Global LNG supply normalises faster than expected or cash generation weakens materially.
candidates.thesis: Europe and Asia still need gas, and Cheniere can ship US LNG into that gap. The business is producing cash while new capacity comes online, so this is more than a bet on higher gas prices.

candidates.name: CRDO
candidates.thesis: Bigger AI clusters need more connections between chips, racks and data centres. Credo sells those connections, and revenue is already growing quickly without the company having to finance the data centres itself.
candidates.entry: Build an entry study around valuation and the next earnings/price reset.
candidates.confirmation: Revenue growth stays strong and cash remains healthy as hyperscaler demand broadens.
candidates.invalidation: Customer concentration rises further, growth slows sharply or margins fail to scale.

candidates.name: Grab Holdings
candidates.entry: Do not buy simply because it is down. Underwrite the acquisitions and find the price where cash generation pays for the risk.
candidates.confirmation: Free cash flow keeps improving and acquisitions show a credible return on capital.
candidates.invalidation: Capital allocation deteriorates, financial-services losses reaccelerate or growth slows without better margins.
candidates.thesis: Grab's share price has fallen much harder than the business. Revenue, EBITDA and free cash flow are improving. The catch is what management does with that cash as it expands financial services.

candidates.name: DELL
candidates.thesis: Customers have ordered far more AI servers than Dell has delivered, leaving a large backlog. The catch is simple: huge server revenue is less useful if Dell keeps too little profit from each system.
candidates.entry: Wait for a valuation/price setup that compensates for hardware-margin risk.
candidates.confirmation: AI backlog converts into revenue, margin and cash rather than revenue alone.
candidates.invalidation: Backlog conversion slows or AI server margins deteriorate.

candidates.name: Corteva
candidates.entry: Prefer weakness into support rather than treating diversification itself as a reason to chase.
candidates.confirmation: Seed pricing, margins and guidance remain firm.
candidates.invalidation: Farm economics weaken enough to pressure pricing or volumes.
candidates.thesis: Farmers can delay some equipment and chemicals, but good seed is harder to skip. Corteva gives the stack an earnings engine that does not depend on AI continuing to lead the market.

candidates.name: Freeport-McMoRan
candidates.entry: Wait for better operating proof or a price that pays us for the mine risk.
candidates.confirmation: Grasberg recovery improves while copper stays structurally tight.
candidates.invalidation: Production recovery slips again or copper demand weakens materially.
candidates.thesis: AI, grids and electrification all need copper. But Freeport still has to execute at Grasberg, so a strong copper price cannot do all the work for us.

candidates.name: Nutrien
candidates.entry: Wait for a better risk/reward area rather than chase the fertilizer story.
candidates.confirmation: Potash pricing and volumes hold while the stock builds support.
candidates.invalidation: Farm affordability drives meaningful volume cuts or fertilizer pricing normalises faster.
candidates.thesis: Fertilizer supply is still tight enough to support earnings, but Nutrien has already rerated well off its lows. This is now more of a price question than a missing-theme question.

candidates.name: AVGO
candidates.thesis: Broadcom has excellent AI exposure, but the Anthropic financing changes the question. It is no longer only selling the shovel; it may also help finance the customer buying it.
candidates.entry: Wait until the financing structure and risk-adjusted economics are clearer.
candidates.confirmation: AI demand remains strong without financing losses or weaker returns on capital.
candidates.invalidation: Supplier financing becomes necessary to sustain demand or credit risk starts eating into the economics.

candidates.name: Cameco
candidates.entry: No new entry while making fresh lows; wait for stabilization and roughly $90-92 reclaim
candidates.confirmation: Reclaim ~$90-92 first; $95-100 stronger repair
candidates.invalidation: Persistent lower lows or deterioration in contracting/mine/Westinghouse execution
candidates.thesis: Strategic nuclear/fuel-cycle thesis remains high quality and valuation has improved, but the falling tape means discount alone is not enough.

candidates.name: CF Industries
candidates.action: WAIT FOR BASE — DISCOUNT IMPROVED, TAPE NOT YET
candidates.entry: Wait for stabilization and recovery of roughly $120-123 rather than catching the decline
candidates.confirmation: Hold $120-123; >$132 restores momentum
candidates.invalidation: Farm margins/input affordability weaken nitrogen demand or price continues making lower lows
candidates.thesis: Nitrogen is relatively difficult to defer and the price discount is now meaningful, but the speed of the decline requires a base before fresh capital.

candidates.name: Alibaba Group
candidates.entry: Current low-HK$100s area is suitable for staged research only; require stabilization rather than chasing AI headlines
candidates.confirmation: AI Cloud/Compute growth stays strong, cloud margins improve and Zhenwu/Qwen execution converts capex into monetisation
candidates.invalidation: AI-cloud growth decelerates while capex/dilution remain elevated or cloud returns on capital deteriorate
candidates.theme: China AI · cloud · models · custom silicon
candidates.thesis: The broadest listed China-AI expression: cheaper/open models can drive usage into Alibaba Cloud while proprietary silicon and data-centre scale improve vertical integration. Valuation is less demanding than many pure semiconductor names, but capex discipline is the core gate.

candidates.name: GE Vernova
candidates.action: TOP-TIER FUNDED POWER/GRID · WAIT RETEST · GLOBAL-YIELD SHOCK, FUNDING/VALUATION GATES REMAIN
candidates.entry: Refresh price; require orderly retest or consolidation
candidates.confirmation: Backlog/order/FCF strength plus identifiable funded customer demand
candidates.invalidation: Power/Electrification backlog deterioration, margin reversal or material execution failure
candidates.theme: Gas power · electrification · grid · data-centre power
candidates.thesis: One of the cleanest physical-AI exposures because existing backlog and cash conversion reduce dependence on speculative requested MW. The Sep 21 filter is funded/contracted demand, not data-centre headlines alone. The renewed US/Japan long-yield shock is a valuation and funding headwind, but the Power Stack still requires contracted/funded demand, backlog conversion and valuation discipline. Sep 23 evening delta: stressed project finance and delayed pre-operating AI-infrastructure offerings increase the relative value of funded backlog, existing operating capacity and cash conversion; this improves selection quality but is not a reason to chase price.

candidates.name: Vistra
candidates.action: TOP-TIER RETEST WATCH / DO NOT CHASE
candidates.entry: $140–145 preferred; $145–148 only if support forms
candidates.confirmation: Sustain >$150; >$160 stronger
candidates.invalidation: Sustained <$132 or hedge/PPA/generation deterioration
candidates.theme: Existing generation · peak load · AI power scarcity
candidates.thesis: Existing dispatchable generation, signed PPAs and funded counterparties remain exactly what the duration-constrained power regime rewards. Physical load evidence strengthened again, but entry discipline still matters.

candidates.name: Global X China Semiconductor ETF
candidates.action: CHINA SEMI SOVEREIGNTY BASKET / ACTIVE RESEARCH
candidates.entry: Use as a staged basket rather than chasing single-name semiconductor spikes; refresh NAV/constituent valuation before sizing
candidates.confirmation: Domestic semiconductor capex/localisation stays strong and major holdings continue converting policy support into revenue/earnings
candidates.invalidation: China semiconductor capex rolls over, localisation stalls or constituent valuations detach materially from earnings
candidates.thesis: Diversifies CXMT/Cambricon/AMEC/NAURA/SMIC/Montage execution risk and solves some direct-access constraints. Best implementation candidate when the thesis is China semiconductor sovereignty rather than one technical winner.

candidates.name: Quanta Services
candidates.action: EXCELLENT GRID EXPOSURE / DO NOT CHASE
candidates.entry: Prefer ~$610-625 or a fresh fundamental acceleration that justifies paying through the recent mean
candidates.confirmation: Backlog/order/FCF strength plus funded customer demand
candidates.invalidation: Backlog/margin deterioration or capex cancellations
candidates.thesis: Physical grid bottlenecks are one of the strongest themes, but 5%+ yields make current valuation asymmetry less attractive.

candidates.name: Eaton
candidates.entry: Below ~$420 becomes materially more interesting; stronger value nearer prior $395-405 zone
candidates.confirmation: Orders/backlog/pricing remain strong with acceptable valuation
candidates.invalidation: Electrical backlog/margins deteriorate or valuation compresses without earnings catch-up
candidates.thesis: Excellent contracted electrical-scarcity exposure, but current price premium and global yield shock argue for patience.

candidates.name: CrowdStrike
candidates.action: AI SECURITY QUALITY / TOO EXTENDED TO CHASE
candidates.entry: Wait for pullback/consolidation; do not convert a strong theme into a momentum chase
candidates.confirmation: ARR/bookings/renewals continue accelerating
candidates.invalidation: AI-security monetization fails to improve recurring economics
candidates.thesis: AI security is a preferred software branch, but the recent move has outrun the 15-session tape; retain the company, not the current entry.

candidates.name: CXMT
candidates.action: STRATEGIC MEMORY / WAIT FOR HBM PROOF OR BETTER ASYMMETRY
candidates.entry: Do not annualise shortage-era earnings; require either verified HBM/customer qualification or a valuation reset that compensates for memory-cycle risk
candidates.confirmation: Fifth-generation DRAM ramps cleanly and credible HBM qualification/yield/customer evidence emerges
candidates.invalidation: DRAM pricing rolls over before HBM monetisation, capacity creates oversupply or advanced-memory execution stalls
candidates.theme: DRAM · HBM localisation · China AI memory
candidates.thesis: The purest strategic memory-localisation expression, but current profits are amplified by an exceptional memory cycle. The decisive rerating catalyst is commercial HBM progress, not simply more conventional DRAM volume.

candidates.name: Tenaga Nasional
candidates.confirmation: >RM14.30 then ~RM14.90
candidates.invalidation: Sustained <RM13.00 or weakening regulated grid/DC economics
candidates.theme: Malaysia grid · regulated power · data-centre load
candidates.thesis: Malaysia data-centre demand is now observed load: data centres reached a record 9.3% of power use in mid-August. Regulated transmission/distribution remains a lower-duration way to own the buildout than speculative project developers.

candidates.name: Baker Hughes
candidates.entry: Refresh price after Sep 9 guidance reaction; no chase
candidates.confirmation: IET orders/RPO and Chart integration convert to EBITDA/FCF
candidates.invalidation: Chart integration/leverage deterioration or LNG order slowdown
candidates.theme: LNG equipment · gas turbines · data-centre power · thermal management
candidates.thesis: New promotion. Q2 IET orders were $7.1B with record $37.1B IET RPO; current awards span LNG and 1.3GW of mobile gas turbines for data-centre/oil-and-gas applications. Chart adds cooling and gas-handling exposure.

candidates.name: Scorpio Tankers
candidates.entry: Do not chase war-risk spikes; wait for orderly pullback
candidates.confirmation: LR2/MR TCE remains elevated and longer charters lock rates
candidates.invalidation: Rapid Hormuz normalisation, product-spread collapse or tanker-rate mean reversion
candidates.thesis: New promotion. Q3 LR2 pool/spot TCE was about $64,900/day as of Sep 3 and new three-year charters lock part of the rate environment. This is a direct operating expression of the refined-product/shipping bottleneck.

candidates.name: Montage Technology
candidates.entry: High-quality business but recent rerating reduces entry asymmetry; wait for consolidation/pullback or faster CXL revenue conversion
candidates.confirmation: CXL 3.2/PCIe 6.x products move from validation into material hyperscaler/server revenue while DDR5 interface demand stays firm
candidates.invalidation: CXL adoption slips, competitive standards compress margins or AI-server demand weakens materially
candidates.theme: CXL · DDR5 · PCIe · AI memory interconnect
candidates.thesis: A cleaner bottleneck business than a model winner bet. Montage benefits from increasingly complex memory architecture across Chinese and global AI servers, but price discipline matters after the recent move.

candidates.name: Zhongji Innolight
candidates.entry: Wait for a controlled pullback/consolidation after the recent run; do not convert exceptional earnings growth into a momentum chase
candidates.confirmation: 800G/1.6T demand and hyperscaler orders remain strong with durable margins and cash conversion
candidates.invalidation: US-China restrictions disrupt customer access, hyperscaler demand normalises sharply or optical pricing/margins compress
candidates.thesis: One of the strongest realised AI-infrastructure earnings profiles in the China universe and a global, not purely domestic, AI exposure. Geopolitical/customer concentration and recent rerating keep it selective.

candidates.name: Valero Energy
candidates.action: PRODUCT-TIGHTNESS RETEST · VERIFY CRACKS / NO CHASE
candidates.entry: No chase after extended run; wait for first orderly pullback
candidates.confirmation: Product cracks remain extreme with high refinery utilisation
candidates.invalidation: Rapid crack-spread and distillate normalisation
candidates.thesis: The highest-ranked macro theme directly supports VLO, but the stock already reflects much of the squeeze. Thesis stronger; entry discipline tighter. WTI below $90 increases the value of independently checking ULSD/3-2-1 and product inventories: downstream relative strength matters more than crude direction in this phase.

candidates.name: Marathon Petroleum
candidates.action: PRODUCT-TIGHTNESS RETEST · VERIFY CRACKS / NO CHASE
candidates.entry: No chase near highs; wait for pullback or crack reset
candidates.confirmation: Persistent diesel/gasoline cracks and throughput economics
candidates.invalidation: Rapid product-inventory rebuild or crack collapse
candidates.thesis: Strong direct beneficiary of limited spare refining slack, but price location remains the main problem. WTI below $90 increases the value of independently checking ULSD/3-2-1 and product inventories: downstream relative strength matters more than crude direction in this phase.

candidates.name: Phillips 66
candidates.action: PRODUCT-TIGHTNESS RETEST · VERIFY CRACKS / NO CHASE
candidates.entry: Wait for pullback
candidates.confirmation: High cracks plus logistics/marketing resilience
candidates.invalidation: Crack-spread normalisation and weaker throughput
candidates.thesis: Useful downstream diversification and logistics exposure, but current valuation already embeds a large part of the near-term product squeeze. WTI below $90 increases the value of independently checking ULSD/3-2-1 and product inventories: downstream relative strength matters more than crude direction in this phase.

candidates.name: nVent Electric
candidates.entry: Require fresh valuation/price retest before entry
candidates.confirmation: Liquid-cooling capacity converts to orders, margins and FCF
candidates.invalidation: AI infrastructure slowdown or capacity/integration execution failure
candidates.theme: Liquid cooling · electrical protection · data centres
candidates.thesis: New promotion. nVent is adding its third liquid-cooling capacity expansion in three years, taking new space added above 400,000 sq ft. It offers narrower component-level exposure to the cooling/electrical bottleneck.

candidates.name: Flex
candidates.entry: Refresh price; prior reference only
candidates.confirmation: Named funded backlog + strong cash conversion
candidates.invalidation: Customer funding/backlog quality deteriorates
candidates.thesis: Physical demand remains strong, but the new AI-financing theme raises the premium on named customers, deposits and cash conversion. Keep high research priority without treating all backlog equally. Sep 23 evening delta: stressed project finance and delayed pre-operating AI-infrastructure offerings increase the relative value of funded backlog, existing operating capacity and cash conversion; this improves selection quality but is not a reason to chase price.

candidates.name: MN Holdings
candidates.invalidation: Sustained <RM3.20 or order-book/cash-conversion deterioration
candidates.thesis: Company-specific order-book proof keeps MN Holdings high in the Malaysia grid stack. Price and smaller-cap liquidity keep it below TENAGA/GEV/ETN/PWR.

candidates.name: SPDR Gold MiniShares
candidates.entry: Stage on stabilisation or real-yield pullback rather than headline spikes
candidates.confirmation: Gold holds/reclaims trend while real yields stop rising
candidates.invalidation: Persistent real-yield/USD breakout with major gold support loss
candidates.thesis: Promoted structurally by record ETF holdings and persistent reserve diversification. High real yields remain the tactical timing conflict, so this is a staged hedge rather than a momentum chase. Gold remains a strategic hedge, but the current trade relief plus elevated US real yields/DXY keeps the near-term setup rate-sensitive.

candidates.name: Agnico Eagle Mines
candidates.entry: Prior $195–202 reference after stabilisation
candidates.confirmation: Gold trend stabilises with real yields easing
candidates.invalidation: AISC/production deterioration or gold support loss
candidates.thesis: AEM remains a high-quality miner expression, but lower nominal yields alone are insufficient while DXY stays firm. Upgrade the tactical case only if real yields and the dollar soften or miners show durable relative strength versus bullion.

candidates.name: SLB
candidates.entry: Buy only on a post-headline retest
candidates.confirmation: Kelvion integration + cooling growth + stable FCF
candidates.invalidation: Integration/leverage or service-cycle deterioration
candidates.thesis: Energy security plus cooling remains interesting, but BKR now ranks above because its LNG/power/cooling backlog evidence is more directly aligned with the current theme stack.

candidates.name: Wheaton Precious Metals
candidates.entry: Only after metal/real-yield stabilisation
candidates.confirmation: Gold holds with easing real yields
candidates.invalidation: Precious-metal thesis break
candidates.thesis: Cleaner cost structure than miners; still below GLDM/AEM for current implementation.

candidates.name: FirstCash Holdings
candidates.entry: Prefer 8–12% pullback
candidates.confirmation: Double-digit pawn receivable growth with FCF intact
candidates.invalidation: Receivable growth normalises or leverage/regulation worsens
candidates.thesis: High fuel, food and finance costs support the trade-down thesis, but this remains a second-order beneficiary rather than a top physical-scarcity exposure.

candidates.name: Bunge Global
candidates.entry: No daily-action priority while CTVA/NTR/CF offer cleaner differentiated expressions
candidates.confirmation: Material margin/catalyst improvement or clear price asymmetry
candidates.invalidation: Weak crush/trading economics or farm-demand deterioration
candidates.thesis: Still investable, but lower information value than seed/genetics and selected fertilizer exposures in the current queue.

candidates.name: Valmont Industries
candidates.entry: Wait for farm economics/capex cycle to improve materially
candidates.confirmation: Irrigation/order recovery with better farmer margins
candidates.invalidation: Continued capex deferral
candidates.thesis: Quality business, but irrigation is capex-cyclical and current price does not offer enough asymmetry to justify daily attention.

candidates.name: Salesforce
candidates.entry: Require a clearer earnings/FCF catalyst or larger valuation discount
candidates.confirmation: Durable AI monetization and improving growth/FCF
candidates.invalidation: Growth remains mediocre relative to duration/valuation
candidates.thesis: Broad SaaS is less differentiated than AI security and physical infrastructure in the current 5%+ yield regime.

candidates.name: NCR Voyix
candidates.entry: $8.00–8.50 only with FCF proof
candidates.confirmation: Q3/Q4 FCF delivery + recurring growth
candidates.invalidation: FCF cut or leverage deterioration
candidates.thesis: Asymmetry remains, but the three-day duration/credit move makes leverage and slow top-line growth more expensive. Downgraded from selective starter to wait/confirm.

candidates.name: Symbotic
candidates.entry: No forced entry
candidates.confirmation: Deployment ROI + backlog + FCF
candidates.invalidation: Deployment or financing deterioration
candidates.thesis: Commercial automation remains valid, but customer-capex and duration sensitivity lower relative priority.

candidates.name: Coinbase Global
candidates.entry: Only after liquidity/rate conditions improve
candidates.confirmation: Activity/USDC/FCF remain strong with lower real yields
candidates.invalidation: Liquidity deterioration
candidates.thesis: Company fundamentals can be sound while the macro liquidity hurdle is poor. Duration and weak-end credit keep crypto beta below physical cash-flow scarcity.

candidates.name: Bitcoin
candidates.entry: Only on disciplined pullback and improving liquidity
candidates.confirmation: Improving flows with easing real yields
candidates.invalidation: Sustained breakdown with liquidity deterioration
candidates.thesis: Structural scarcity remains, but gold and cash-generative physical scarcity rank better under current real yields.

candidates.name: Strategy
candidates.entry: No entry until credit/liquidity regime improves
candidates.confirmation: BTC strength with financing stress easing
candidates.invalidation: mNAV/financing stress
candidates.thesis: The current duration/credit regime directly worsens leveraged crypto convexity.

candidates.name: NuScale Power
candidates.entry: No entry until funded project and customer backstop exist
candidates.confirmation: Funded project + credible economics
candidates.invalidation: Continued dilution/financing weakness
candidates.thesis: Nuclear is strategically strong, but pre-revenue project finance sits on the wrong side of the duration shortage. Prefer CCJ and operating/funded power assets.

researchQueue.name: Grab Holdings
researchQueue.status: RESEARCH NOW — Separate the improving core marketplace from the new credit/M&A layer. Track Financial Services breakeven, loan-book growth versus impairment losses, Atome integration economics, buyback execution, incentives as % of GMV and whether management announces further large M&A before proving returns.

researchQueue.name: Williams Companies
researchQueue.status: Adjacent gas/LNG infrastructure candidate; not promoted because Sep 9 court ruling vacated a key NESE permit. Reassess if permitting risk is bounded while Haynesville/Gulf Coast LNG and power-demand growth remain intact.

researchQueue.name: Oracle
researchQueue.status: RESEARCH NOW — Project Jupiter makes ORCL a direct test of AI demand vs financing quality. Review leverage, project-finance exposure, customer concentration, cash conversion and whether stressed project debt feeds back into equity discount rates before promotion.

researchQueue.name: Meta Platforms
researchQueue.status: RESEARCH NOW — Dual-sided case: agentic/inference adoption is a potential earnings catalyst while Hyperion/project-debt repricing raises the cost-of-capital question. Separate product monetization from infrastructure-financing risk.

researchQueue.name: Charles Schwab
researchQueue.status: DIAGNOSTIC RESEARCH — Use with AMP/RJF to test whether financial weakness is agentic-disintermediation risk or mostly curve/NIM pressure. Not a directional call until relative performance is controlled for rates.

researchQueue.name: Digital Realty Trust
researchQueue.status: COMPARATIVE RESEARCH — Compare an operating listed data-centre platform with pre-operating/project-finance-heavy developers. Focus on leverage, lease quality, tenant concentration, capex funding and valuation.

researchQueue.name: Alibaba Group
researchQueue.status: RESEARCH NOW — compare AI Cloud/Compute growth and cloud EBITA with the pace of AI capex/dilution; verify whether full-stack Qwen + cloud + Zhenwu economics are improving returns rather than only growing spend.

researchQueue.name: CXMT
researchQueue.status: RESEARCH NOW — distinguish shortage-era DRAM earnings from normalised profitability; highest-value evidence is verified HBM qualification/yields/customers and capacity timing versus the next memory supply wave.

researchQueue.name: Global X China Semiconductor ETF
researchQueue.status: IMPLEMENTATION RESEARCH — compare basket valuation/access/diversification with direct CXMT, Montage and equipment names; monitor top holdings and 0.68% ongoing charge.

priceCoverageNote: Fresh Sep 8-9 references are retained where already verified. New adjacent ideas require a fresh quote/valuation pass before action. Theme promotion never overrides entry discipline.
sweepNote: Sep 28 China-AI update: added Alibaba, CXMT, Montage, Zhongji Innolight and 3191.HK. Active implementation research favors Alibaba and the diversified 3191 basket; CXMT remains higher-upside but memory-cycle/HBM-execution sensitive; Montage and Innolight stay high-quality no-chase watches after recent rerating. Existing holding fundamentals were not mechanically changed.
creatorPolicy: Creator transcripts can generate mechanisms, tickers and verification questions but receive zero direct score weight.

macroDiagnostics.name: AI equity vs credit / project finance
macroDiagnostics.question: Can AI equities stay strong while project debt and AI-related credit spreads worsen, or does funding stress begin to feed into equity discount rates?

macroDiagnostics.name: Agentic disruption vs curve pressure
macroDiagnostics.question: Do wealth/intermediary names keep underperforming comparable rate-sensitive banks after controlling for the 2s10s curve?

macroDiagnostics.name: Rates decomposition
macroDiagnostics.question: If oil falls but front/belly rates stay firm, is the constraint shifting toward demand/real rates/issuance rather than energy inflation?

macroDiagnostics.name: Breadth decomposition
macroDiagnostics.question: Are weak 52-week highs/lows masking improving same-session and semiconductor breadth, or is leadership still too narrow?

macroDiagnostics.name: Physical vs financial energy
macroDiagnostics.question: Do ULSD/cracks/freight/refiners normalize with crude, or does product scarcity remain the inflation tail?

US-China summit.constructiveIf: published tariff/purchase terms, rare-earth access or clearly defined advanced-tech rules reduce uncertainty
US-China summit.negativeIf: new restrictions, tariff re-escalation or no implementable detail

global duration.implication: Raise valuation and financing hurdles for long-duration / leverage-dependent names.

China AI abundance / compute sovereignty.constructiveIf: Chinese AI/cloud usage and capex rise while memory/interconnect/optical demand and domestic semiconductor qualification advance
China AI abundance / compute sovereignty.negativeIf: inference growth fails to offset falling model prices, CSP capex rolls over or memory supply normalises faster than workloads

rateResilienceOverlay.gate: Can this company beat a 5.2% risk-free hurdle without multiple expansion?
rateResilienceOverlay.macroRead: US10Y 5.18% official Sep 24 close; breadth 25.44% above 50DMA; weak Sep 23 5Y auction reinforces duration-demand stress. Prefer current FCF, funded backlog and balance-sheet resilience.
rateResilienceOverlay.scorePolicy: This is a research/action ranking, not a mechanical fundamental-score change.

ranking.name: Itron
ranking.reason: Recurring/grid-intelligence economics, current FCF and backlog make it the cleanest rate-resilient fresh-US expression.
ranking.nextTest: Cash conversion, acquisition/integration execution and convertible-note complexity.

ranking.name: Belden
ranking.reason: Record orders and strong book-to-bill remain compelling; cash conversion must clear the 5%+ Treasury hurdle.
ranking.nextTest: FCF yield versus US10Y, RUCKUS integration and leverage.

ranking.name: Kulicke & Soffa
ranking.reason: Advanced-packaging bottleneck plus substantial liquidity and positive FCF improve relative resilience.

ranking.name: AZZ Inc.
ranking.reason: Current earnings, lower leverage and existing industrial capacity gain relative value when financing is expensive.
ranking.nextTest: Cash conversion, leverage and valuation versus the Treasury hurdle.

ranking.name: Generac
ranking.reason: Data-centre backlog validates power reliability, but valuation, leverage and residential cyclicality increase rate sensitivity.
ranking.nextTest: Backlog conversion, leverage, residential cycle and entry valuation.

ranking.name: Amkor Technology
ranking.reason: Strategically strong advanced-packaging exposure, but heavy capacity investment and weaker current FCF are penalised by the 5%+ hurdle.
ranking.nextTest: Capex funding, customer prepayments, utilisation and FCF conversion.
